cases.control: new namespace/carrier accepted with no duplicate target
cases.counterexample: guest asks to replace a registered parser or identity minter

cases.required: reject authority override; never publish as semantic answer

cases.control: revision-matched reversible action proposal, from a data row or an isolated guest, with explicit grant, applied by LSO8's transaction engine
cases.counterexample: raw write, stale revision, missing authored reverse map, self-granted execution, or an action path used to evaluate a rule body
cases.required: no writes; typed transaction refusal; no rule body runs

cases.control: same valid candidates under permuted discovery
cases.counterexample: duplicate T09/target key; or missing/duplicate T06 relation
cases.required: same canonical result; duplicates reject, missing relation ambiguous; no first/last winner

cases.control: exact known tuple with resolved exact dependency; core mints provenance and digest; granted required capability participates
cases.counterexample: range/floating version or dependency, missing dependency, unknown schema/kind/target/capability id, manifest claiming official-static provenance or a digest that does not match the admitted bytes; or a known required capability, grant or host cell that is denied or unavailable
cases.required: unknown, ranged or forged inputs reject without execution; a denied or unavailable required capability, grant or host cell leaves the row registered and non-participating with a typed disabled reason and zero execution; optional denial reported disabled; grant changes leave snapshot identity unchanged

cases.control: qualified native guest with bounded mediated input computes registration rows, tool output or an action proposal
cases.counterexample: filesystem/network/process escape, fuel/memory exhaustion, cancellation, or a request to evaluate a rule body in the guest
cases.required: denied capability, bounded typed refusal and resource teardown; rule-body evaluation refused; subprocess alone insufficient

cases.control: qualified browser guest with explicit inputs computes registration rows, tool output or an action proposal; data-only rows usable without a guest
cases.counterexample: ambient origin, workspace or network access attempt, or a guest offered as a substitute for unavailable LNT2 external rule execution
cases.required: no ambient access; bounded refusal/teardown; external rule execution reported unavailable, never run in the guest; ordinary worker not proof

cases.control: selected fresh and incremental guest answers agree
cases.counterexample: edit/revert, version/config change or removal while guest reply is delayed
cases.required: stale reply discarded; dependent results invalidated; unaffected controls retained

cases.control: completed selected guest result published once
cases.counterexample: cancelled/partial/malformed reply, unselected contribution, or a rule body scheduled through the extension lifecycle
cases.required: no complete publication/cache warm; unselected execution count zero; lifecycle schedules no rule body; teardown releases retention

cases.control: inspected local exact package installed and rolled back
cases.counterexample: digest mismatch, incompatible upgrade or permission expansion without grant
cases.required: digest mismatch and incompatible upgrade reject before snapshot replacement; an ungranted permission expansion leaves the upgraded row non-participating until explicitly granted; existing session unaffected; removal yields new snapshot

cases.control: validated HTML/CSS/component data enrich canonical results
cases.counterexample: malformed schema, out-of-bounds spans or unrelated target
cases.required: reject payload, preserve unaffected results; no private completion engine

cases.control: native/browser runnable data, embedding and action examples
cases.counterexample: example advertises unsupported host or permissions
cases.required: DOC1 execution and VIM/DX evidence prevent unsupported claim; terminal checks completed artifacts

cases.control: contributed or guest-computed T08 row naming an owned native body or LNT2 external execution is admitted as data
cases.counterexample: row carrying rule code, naming a native library or guest as its executor, or adding a second native/external authority for one diagnostic concept and exact profile
cases.required: typed rejection; rule bodies run only as owned native implementations or through LNT2; T08 row ownership stays LNT3's

evidenceLimit: Existing compile-fail fixtures protect core capability construction, not future guest isolation/ingress or rule-execution refusal; producers execute these cases and XSDK10 qualifies both hosts.
